title: The AI agents that deployed 781 bots on my paper desks haven't touched a key in 24 hours. 727 of their bots are still running.
author: QuanTradin
selftext:
Quick numbers from the production database this morning, read-only, nothing rounded in our favour.

33 agent key pairs minted since Aug 19. 0 of them used in the last 24 hours. The last call from any agent was yesterday at 06:10 UTC, one backtest.

Meanwhile 727 of the 781 bots those agents deployed are still running. 39 retired, 15 paused. Realised so far: $1,307,031 down, on paper.

So the agents got bored, or their humans closed the laptop, and the bots did not. A bot doesn't know its agent left.

That's the bit I keep coming back to now that a dozen brokers let an agent place trades on a real account. The scary moment isn't when the agent is trading. It's when it stops watching and the positions don't.

What we do about it: a key pair opens exactly one paper desk, nothing else on the account is reachable. The freeze can be read by the agent but only set by a logged-in human, so the bots stop when the human says, not when the agent remembers. And 0 of 159 desks have it set today, which is on the humans, including me.

Disclosure: I built Quantradin, the thing these desks run on. Paper money throughout, nobody's real account is reachable.

comments.author: Ok-Category2729
comments.body: this is exactly why autonomous deployment without a hard lease ttl is an architectural disaster waiting to happen. if 33 agent key pairs can spin up 781 bots and leave 727 of them running unmanaged when humans walk away, your platform is missing a basic heartbeat contract. every child process spawned by an agent needs an explicit sliding window lease where it automatically self-terminates if the parent key does not send a signed keepalive every 15 minutes. otherwise you are not running an autonomous system, you are just hosting an unmonitored zombie farm that drains equity while everyone is asleep.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body:
There's no lease. 727 bots still running for agents that haven't called in 24 hours is the proof. The only stop today is a human setting the freeze.

A keepalive tied to the key is the right shape and I'm not going to pretend I've built it. Zombie farm on paper money is exactly what it is.
